title: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia / small lymphocytic lymphoma
subtitle: CD5+ CD23+ B-cell neoplasm · treat only on an iwCLL indication · TP53 + IGHV pick between continuous BTKi and fixed-duration venetoclax · chemoimmunotherapy is obsolete for most
source: Compiled from iwCLL 2018 · NCCN · WHO-HEM5/ICC 2022 · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Diagnosis — CLL vs SLL vs MBL (iwCLL 2018, WHO-5)
rows: ≥5×109/L clonal B cells in blood, sustained ≥3 mo; clonality by light-chain restriction on flow. A cytopenia from typical marrow infiltrate = CLL at any count
Same disease, nodal: nodes and/or spleen, blood B cells <5×109/L, no marrow-driven cytopenia; confirm on lymph node biopsy

Clonal B cells <5×109/L, no nodes, organomegaly, cytopenia or symptoms. Low-count <0.5 (rarely progresses) vs high-count 0.5–4.9. Progression to treatment-requiring CLL ~1–2%/yr; more infections and skin cancers
WHO-5: >15% prolymphocytes in blood/marrow. WHO-5 dropped B-PLL (now CLL with PL progression, MCL variant, or splenic B-cell lymphoma with prominent nucleoli); ICC 2022 keeps B-PLL narrowly
Aggressive lymphoma arising in CLL — DLBCL type (~90%) or Hodgkin type. Page 2

blocks.heading: Flow phenotype and the mimics
items: CD19+ CD5+ CD23+ with dim CD20, dim CD79b, dim surface Ig (single light chain). CD200+, LEF1+, ROR1+; FMC7−. Smudge cells on smear
Matutes (RMH) score: 1 point each for CD5+, CD23+, FMC7−, weak sIg, weak CD22 (CD79b in the modified score). 4–5 = CLL (87% of CLL); 3 = atypical; 0–2 = other B-LPD
Mantle cell is the dangerous mimic (CD5+): CD23−, CD200−, bright sIg/CD20, cyclin D1+, SOX11+, t(11;14). Atypical/CD23-dim cases: cyclin D1 IHC or t(11;14) FISH
Others: marginal zone (CD5−, CD23−), hairy cell (CD11c/CD25/CD103, BRAF V600E), follicular (CD10+)

blocks.heading: Pretreatment workup (iwCLL)
items: Before every line of therapy: FISH (del13q, del11q, +12, del17p) + TP53 sequencing — clones evolve; TP53 status flips the regimen
IGHV mutation status once (doesn't change): unmutated = ≥98% identity to germline; mutated = >2% deviation
CpG-stimulated karyotype: complex = ≥3 abnormalities; ≥5 is independently adverse; 3–4 adverse mainly with TP53 aberration
CBC + smear, CMP, LDH, uric acid, β2-microglobulin, DAT + retic/haptoglobin, quantitative IgG/IgA/IgM, HBV (HBsAg, anti-HBc), HCV, HIV
CT neck/C/A/P before venetoclax (TLS risk) or in trials; not needed for watch-and-wait. PET only if Richter suspected. Marrow not required for diagnosis — do it for unexplained cytopenias
Cardiac history, ECG, BP, anticoagulants/antiplatelets and CYP3A drugs before choosing a BTKi

chains.header: Diagnosis → is there an iwCLL indication?
boxes: CBC q3–6 mo; treating early does not help:
CLL12 ibrutinib vs placebo — EFS gain, no OS
Yes → test TP53 (FISH + seq) and IGHV
then fitness, cardiac risk, drug interactions,
and patient preference: fixed vs continuous
FCR only IGHV-mutated, fit, young — rarely now
allo-HCT if fit — the only curative option

blocks.heading: iwCLL indications to treat — need ≥1
items: Progressive marrow failure: Hb <10 g/dL or platelets <100×109/L (a stable plt just under 100 may be watched)
Spleen ≥6 cm below costal margin, or progressive/symptomatic · nodes ≥10 cm, or progressive/symptomatic
Lymphocyte doubling time <6 mo or ≥50% rise in 2 mo (ALC <30: observe longer before calling LDT)
Autoimmune anemia/ITP poorly responsive to steroids · symptomatic extranodal disease
Constitutional: weight loss ≥10% in 6 mo · fatigue ECOG ≥2 · fever ≥38.0°C ≥2 wk · night sweats ≥1 mo (no infection)
NOT indications: high ALC alone (leukostasis is rare), hypogammaglobulinemia, a paraprotein, adverse FISH/IGHV, Rai stage alone

blocks.heading: Staging
rows: 0 lymphocytosis only (low) · I nodes · II spleen/liver (intermediate) · III Hb <11 · IV plt <100 (high). Original median survival >150 / 101 / 71 / 19 / 19 mo
Areas: head-neck, axillae, groins, spleen, liver. A ≤2 areas (~55%; near-normal survival) · B ≥3 areas (~30%) · C Hb <10 or plt <100 (~15%; median ~2 yr)
blocks.footnote: Anemia/thrombocytopenia from autoimmune destruction does not upstage — Rai III/IV and Binet C mean marrow failure.

blocks.heading: CLL-IPI (2016) — prognosis, not a treatment trigger
rows: Rai I–IV or Binet B–C · age >65
blocks.footnote: Low 0–1 · intermediate 2–3 · high 4–6 · very high 7–10 → 5-yr OS 93 / 79 / 63 / 23% (chemo era; targeted agents narrow the gaps, esp. for IGHV).

blocks.heading: Genetics (Döhner hierarchy)
rows: Most favorable; median OS 133 mo (chemo era)
ATM; bulky nodes; adverse with chemo — largely overcome by BTKi
del(17p) / TP53 mut ~7% at dx; more at relapse
Shorter remissions after fixed-duration and chemo; no plateau with FCR

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — first-line evidence, relapsed disease and sequencing, Richter transformation

blocks.heading: First line — the evidence
rows: ≥65 or comorbid, vs BR: 5-yr median PFS NR vs 44.1 mo, HR 0.29 (IGHV-U 0.21, IGHV-M 0.40); OS no different (85.8 vs 85.0%). Arm C del(17p) (single-arm, n=109): ORR 94.5%, 18-mo PFS 88.6%
Older/comorbid, vs Clb-O: 6-yr PFS 78% (A-O) / 62% (A) / 17%; A-O vs A HR 0.58; OS HR 0.62 A-O vs Clb-O. The one BTKi trial where adding anti-CD20 clearly helps

RESONATE-2 (≥65): median PFS 8.9 vs 1.3 yr vs chlorambucil (~10-yr). A041202 (≥65): 48-mo PFS 76% vs 47% (BR), rituximab adds nothing (HR 1.00), no OS gain; AF 18%, HTN 55%. E1912 (≤70): IR beat FCR, PFS HR 0.37, OS HR 0.47 — incl IGHV-mutated at 5.8 yr
No del(17p), vs BR: PFS HR 0.20, 24-mo PFS 93.4 vs 70.7%. FDA 1L approval 2 Oct 2026 (no del17p). CLL-314 vs ibrutinib: ORR noninferior (87.0 vs 78.5%), PFS still immature
Unfit (CIRS >6 or CrCl <70), vs Clb-O: 6-yr median PFS 76.2 vs 36.4 mo, HR 0.40; OS HR 0.69 (P=.052, NS). Shorter PFS with del(17p), IGHV-U, nodes ≥5 cm
GV / GIV / RV vs FCR-BR: 5-yr PFS 69.8 / 81.3 / 57.4 vs 50.7%; month-15 uMRD GV 86.5% vs 52.0%. Venetoclax-rituximab was not better than CIT — obinutuzumab is the 1L partner. No OS difference
Fit, no del17p/TP53, vs FCR/BR: 36-mo PFS AV 76.5% / AVO 83.1% / 66.5%; AV HR 0.65. AVO had more COVID deaths (25 vs 10) and lower 36-mo OS (87.7 vs 94.1%). FDA Feb 2026 for AV (14 cycles)

GLOW (older/unfit, vs Clb-O): 66-mo PFS 51.7 vs 18.1%, OS HR 0.46. CAPTIVATE (phase 2, ≤70): 24-mo PFS 95%; after uMRD, placebo vs continued ibrutinib 1-yr DFS 95 vs 100% (NS); TP53 36-mo PFS 81%. EU-approved, not FDA-labeled
Fit ≤75: I+V for 2× the time to uMRD (max 6 yr) vs FCR: 5-yr PFS 93.9 vs 58.1%, OS HR 0.26; vs ibrutinib alone PFS HR 0.29, OS HR 0.41. Cardiac SAEs 10.7% vs 0.4% (FCR)
VenO vs I+V vs continuous ibrutinib (n=909): 3-yr PFS 81.1 / 79.4 / 81.0% — both fixed-duration arms noninferior. PB uMRD 73.3 / 47.2 / 0%
MDACC 12.8-yr PFS 53.9% if IGHV-mutated (plateau) vs 8.7% unmutated. Beaten by E1912, FLAIR, CLL13, AMPLIFY; myelosuppression, infections, therapy-related myeloid neoplasms. Never for TP53 or IGHV-U
blocks.footnote: Fixed vs continuous: CLL17 shows equal 3-yr PFS. Fixed duration = drug holiday, less cumulative cardiac/bleeding toxicity, needs TLS ramp-up and infusions (VenO). Continuous = simplest, preferred for TP53, but indefinite cost and AF/HTN. Obinutuzumab, not rituximab, with 1L venetoclax.

blocks.heading: Choosing first line — patient factors
rows: Continuous zanubrutinib or acalabrutinib; VenO if a BTKi is contraindicated (expect shorter PFS)
Fixed duration (VenO or AV) — longest treatment-free intervals; FCR no longer needed
Either: fixed duration (VenO, AV, I+V) or continuous BTKi — CLL17 equal PFS; MRD-guided I+V (FLAIR) for fit
VenO; if a BTKi is needed, zanubrutinib or acalabrutinib, never ibrutinib first
Renal impairment, bulky high-TLS-risk, can't do TLS labs
Continuous BTKi, or a BTKi lead-in before venetoclax (AV, I+V)
Acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib or VenO (CLL14 enrolled CIRS >6)

blocks.heading: Response and MRD
items: iwCLL CR: ALC <4×109/L, nodes <1.5 cm, no hepatosplenomegaly, no B symptoms, ANC ≥1.5, plt ≥100, Hb ≥11 untransfused. Most patients on a BTKi reach PR, not CR — still durable
BTKi redistribution lymphocytosis in the first weeks (cells leave nodes) is expected, not progression

uMRD = <10−4 (1 CLL cell in 10,000) by flow or NGS. Predicts PFS after fixed-duration therapy (MURANO, GLOW, CLL14); meaningless on continuous BTKi (CLL17 0%). MRD-guided duration is a trial/FLAIR concept, not routine

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory — evidence and sequencing
rows: vs BR: median PFS 54.7 vs 17.0 mo; 7-yr OS 69.6 vs 51.0%. uMRD at end of therapy predicts long PFS. VenR retreatment: ORR 72%, median PFS 23 mo. Mostly BTKi-naive patients
del17p/del11q: median PFS 38.4 mo both (noninferior); AF 9.4 vs 16.0%, HTN 9.4 vs 23.2%, any bleeding 38 vs 51%
PFS superior, HR 0.65 (24-mo 78.4 vs 65.9%), incl del17p/TP53 (HR 0.53); AF 2.5 vs 10.1% (interim); fewer fatal cardiac events
All post-cBTKi, vs idelalisib-R/BR: median PFS 14.0 vs 8.7 mo, HR 0.54; OS no different (crossover). Accelerated 2023 → regular approval 3 Dec 2025: R/R after a cBTKi (BCL2i no longer required)
Fixed duration vs VR (80% cBTKi-exposed): 24-mo PFS 87 vs 72%, HR 0.55. Not FDA-approved as of Oct 2026
After BTKi + venetoclax: CR/CRi 18%, ORR 43%, blood uMRD 63%; median PFS 11.9 mo. CRS 85% (gr 3 9%), neurotox 45% (gr 3 18%). Accelerated approval Mar 2024, ≥2 lines incl BTKi + BCL2i
Only curative option; for fit patients with double-exposed/refractory disease or Richter in remission
BTK degraders (BGB-16673, bexobrutideg) and sonrotoclax — trials only (sonrotoclax is FDA-approved for R/R MCL)

blocks.heading: Resistance and sequencing rules
items: Ibrutinib progression: BTK C481 or PLCG2 mutations in ~85%, detectable a median 9.3 mo before clinical relapse. Covalent BTKis share C481 binding → don't swap cBTKi for progression; pirtobrutinib (noncovalent) binds C481-mutant BTK
On pirtobrutinib, non-C481 BTK mutations (T474I, L528W) emerge; L528W and T474I also cross-resist zanubrutinib/acalabrutinib. Venetoclax resistance: BCL2 G101V
Intolerance ≠ resistance: ibrutinib AF/bleeding → switch to acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib
Keep the BTKi going until the next therapy starts — stopping can cause a rapid disease flare
Retest FISH + TP53 at every relapse; new adenopathy with a high LDH → think Richter

blocks.heading: Richter transformation
items: ~2–10% of CLL (~0.5–1%/yr). Suspect with rapid, asymmetric node growth, rising LDH, B symptoms, hypercalcemia, new extranodal disease
PET-CT → biopsy the hottest lesion. SUVmax ≥10 flags Richter (OS 6.9 vs 56.7 mo); core or excisional, not FNA (FNA often nondiagnostic)
Clonally related (same IGHV as the CLL; more TP53 disruption) median OS 14.2 mo vs unrelated 62.5 mo — unrelated behaves like de novo DLBCL
Treatment: R-CHOP-type induction → allo-HCT in responders; CD19 CAR-T or bispecifics on trial/off-label. Hodgkin type: ABVD-type. No Richter-specific FDA approval. Median OS overall ~10 mo

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, TLS, BTKi toxicity, disease complications, key trials

blocks.heading: Regimen dosing
rows: 100 mg BID, continuous; A-O: obinutuzumab C2–7. Tablets OK with PPIs (old capsules: avoid)
160 mg BID or 320 mg daily, continuous
20 → 50 → 100 → 200 → 400 mg, one step per week (5 weeks), with TLS prophylaxis (table)
Obinutuzumab 100 mg C1D1, 900 mg C1D2, 1000 mg C1D8 + D15, then 1000 mg D1 C2–6. Venetoclax ramp starts C1D22, 400 mg from C3, stop after C12
Acalabrutinib 100 mg BID C1–14; venetoclax ramp-up from C3, 400 mg through C14. (AVO adds obinutuzumab C2–7 — not in US label)
Ibrutinib 420 mg ×3 cycles lead-in (debulks: high-TLS-risk 21% → 1%), then + venetoclax ramp to 400 mg ×12 cycles (15 total)
Ramp-up 5 wk, then rituximab 375 mg/m² C1, 500 mg/m² C2–6 (q28d); venetoclax 400 mg for 24 mo from rituximab C1D1
Flu/Cy lymphodepletion → 90–110×106 CAR+ T cells; REMS removed; stay near center, no driving ~2 wk

blocks.heading: Venetoclax TLS risk (label) — reassess after debulking
rows: All nodes <5 cm and ALC <25 → oral fluids 1.5–2 L/d + allopurinol (start 2–3 d before) · outpatient; labs pre, 6–8 h, 24 h at the first 20 and 50 mg doses
Any node 5 to <10 cm or ALC ≥25 → oral ± IV fluids + allopurinol · same labs; consider admission if CrCl <80
Any node ≥10 cm, or ALC ≥25 + any node ≥5 cm → oral + IV fluids 150–200 mL/h, allopurinol, rasburicase if uric acid high · admit for 20 and 50 mg; labs 0, 4, 8, 12, 24 h
blocks.footnote: Labs = K, phos, Ca, uric acid, creatinine — correct before the next dose. Debulk first (BTKi lead-in in GLOW/AMPLIFY; obinutuzumab in VenO). No urine alkalinization.

blocks.heading: Fixed-duration regimens at a glance
rows: 12 cycles (~1 yr) · IV obinutuzumab C1–6 · PB uMRD after therapy 73.3% (CLL17) · 1L, any fitness
14 cycles · all oral · 1L (AMPLIFY excluded del17p/TP53); FDA Feb 2026
15 cycles · all oral · PB uMRD 47.2% (CLL17) · 1L; not US-labeled
blocks.footnote: All need the 5-week venetoclax ramp-up and TLS precautions; BTKi lead-in (AV, I+V) lowers TLS risk category.

blocks.heading: BTK inhibitors compared
rows: Covalent (C481), 1st gen · AF (16.0% in ELEVATE-RR), HTN, ventricular arrhythmia, bleeding, arthralgia
Covalent, more selective · headache early; AF 9.4% vs 16.0%, HTN 9.4 vs 23.2% (vs ibrutinib)
Covalent, more selective · neutropenia; AF 2.5 vs 10.1% vs ibrutinib (ALPINE interim)
Noncovalent · works with C481 mutations; AF/flutter 3.1% (label, pooled); infections, rash

blocks.heading: BTKi toxicity management
items: Atrial fibrillation: rate control (avoid diltiazem/verapamil — CYP3A), DOAC if indicated; often switch to a 2nd-gen BTKi or to venetoclax
Ventricular arrhythmia / sudden death: ibrutinib label warning; FLAIR excess cardiac deaths. Palpitations/syncope → hold + ECG/Holter; don't rechallenge ibrutinib
Hypertension: 55% all-grade on ibrutinib (A041202) — check BP every visit, treat early
Bleeding: no warfarin; avoid fish oil/vitamin E; caution with DOAC + antiplatelet. Hold 3–7 days before and after procedures
Headache with acalabrutinib (31–40%, early, self-limited): acetaminophen + caffeine. Also arthralgia, rash, diarrhea, bruising

CYP3A: acalabrutinib — avoid strong inhibitors, 100 mg daily with moderate · zanubrutinib — 80 mg daily (strong), 80 mg BID (moderate) · pirtobrutinib — minus 50 mg with strong · venetoclax with posaconazole 70 mg, other strong 100 mg, moderate ≥50% cut; strong inhibitors contraindicated during ramp-up

blocks.heading: Complications of the disease
items: Autoimmune cytopenias ~5–10%: AIHA most common (warm IgG), ITP ~2%, PRCA and autoimmune granulocytopenia <1%. Distinguish from marrow failure (retic, haptoglobin, DAT, marrow). Steroids ± rituximab; IVIG for ITP bleeding. Steroid-refractory autoimmune cytopenia = iwCLL indication — treat the CLL (BTKi or VenO; avoid fludarabine monotherapy)

Infection is the leading cause of death: hypogammaglobulinemia + T-cell and neutrophil dysfunction. IVIG if IgG <500 mg/dL + recurrent serious bacterial infections (fewer infections, no survival gain)
Vaccines: before therapy when possible; no live vaccines; recombinant zoster (2 doses), pneumococcal conjugate, influenza, COVID, RSV — responses blunted on BTKi/anti-CD20
Prophylaxis: anti-HBc+ → entecavir with anti-CD20 (HBV reactivation). PJP + HSV/VZV with FCR/BR, idelalisib (label) and after CAR-T; individualize on BTKi/venetoclax
Second cancers: skin SCC, BCC, melanoma, Merkel markedly increased → annual skin exam, sun protection. Acalabrutinib label: second primaries 16% (non-melanoma skin 9%)

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Zanubrutinib vs BR 1L — PFS HR 0.29; del17p arm C works
VenO ×12 vs Clb-O — median PFS 76.2 vs 36.4 mo
GV/GIV beat CIT; RV did not
AV vs FCR/BR — PFS HR 0.65; FDA 2026
I+V vs Clb-O — OS HR 0.46 at 67 mo
MRD-guided I+V vs FCR — OS HR 0.26
VenR vs BR R/R — OS benefit at 7 yr
Early ibrutinib: EFS only, no OS — watch and wait

blocks.heading: On-treatment monitoring
items: Venetoclax neutropenia (gr 3–4 52.8% in CLL14): G-CSF, hold/dose-reduce per label rather than stopping; check CBC each cycle

Obinutuzumab infusion reactions (40% with Clb-O vs 13% when given with acalabrutinib in ELEVATE-TN): split first dose 100/900 mg, premedicate (steroid, acetaminophen, antihistamine), hold antihypertensives the morning of dose 1
BTKi: CBC, BP, pulse every visit; ask about palpitations, bruising, infections. Long-term: ~20% of ibrutinib patients stop for toxicity (E1912: 21.9% by 5.8 yr)
Off therapy (fixed duration or watch-and-wait): CBC + exam q3–6 mo; imaging only for symptoms or before re-treatment

BTK inhibitors compared Agent Binding · signature toxicity Ibrutinib Covalent (C481), 1st gen · AF (16.0% in ELEVATE-RR), HTN , ventricular arrhythmia, bleeding, arthralgia Acalabrutinib Covalent, more selective · headache early; AF 9.4% vs 16.0%, HTN 9.4 vs 23.2% (vs ibrutinib) Zanubrutinib Covalent, more selective · neutropenia ; AF 2.5 vs 10.1% vs ibrutinib (ALPINE interim) Pirtobrutinib Noncovalent · works with C481 mutations; AF/flutter 3.1% (label, pooled); infections, rash BTKi toxicity management Atrial fibrillation: rate control ( avoid diltiazem/verapamil — CYP3A), DOAC if indicated; often switch to a 2nd-gen BTKi or to venetoclax Ventricular arrhythmia / sudden death: ibrutinib label warning; FLAIR excess cardiac deaths. Palpitations/syncope → hold + ECG/Holter; don't rechallenge ibrutinib Hypertension: 55% all-grade on ibrutinib (A041202) — check BP every visit, treat early Bleeding: no warfarin ; avoid fish oil/vitamin E; caution with DOAC + antiplatelet. Hold 3–7 days before and after procedures Headache with acalabrutinib (31–40%, early, self-limited): acetaminophen + caffeine. Also arthralgia, rash, diarrhea, bruising CYP3A: acalabrutinib — avoid strong inhibitors, 100 mg daily with moderate · zanubrutinib — 80 mg daily (strong), 80 mg BID (moderate) · pirtobrutinib — minus 50 mg with strong · venetoclax with posaconazole 70 mg , other strong 100 mg, moderate ≥50% cut; strong inhibitors contraindicated during ramp-up Complications of the disease Autoimmune cytopenias ~5–10%: AIHA most common (warm IgG), ITP ~2%, PRCA and autoimmune granulocytopenia <1%. Distinguish from marrow failure (retic, haptoglobin, DAT, marrow). Steroids ± rituximab ; IVIG for ITP bleeding. Steroid-refractory autoimmune cytopenia = iwCLL indication — treat the CLL (BTKi or VenO; avoid fludarabine monotherapy ) Infection is the leading cause of death: hypogammaglobulinemia + T-cell and neutrophil dysfunction. IVIG if IgG <500 mg/dL + recurrent serious bacterial infections (fewer infections, no survival gain) Vaccines: before therapy when possible; no live vaccines ; recombinant zoster (2 doses), pneumococcal conjugate, influenza, COVID, RSV — responses blunted on BTKi/anti-CD20 Prophylaxis: anti-HBc+ → entecavir with anti-CD20 (HBV reactivation). PJP + HSV/VZV with FCR/BR, idelalisib (label) and after CAR-T; individualize on BTKi/venetoclax Second cancers: skin SCC, BCC, melanoma, Merkel markedly increased → annual skin exam , sun protection.
